instructions: Hinge into a stable position with the elbow beside the torso. Extend the elbow against the cable without moving the shoulder, then return slowly.

name: Rolling Dumbbell Triceps Extension
description: A lying dumbbell extension combining elbow flexion with a controlled upper-arm rollback.
instructions: Lower the dumbbells near the shoulders as the elbows bend, then let the upper arms roll slightly back. Reverse the motion and extend the elbows without dropping the weights toward the face.

name: Tate Press
description: A lying dumbbell triceps exercise with the elbows held outward.
instructions: Hold the dumbbells above the chest with a comfortable grip. Bend the elbows outward to bring the weights toward the chest without impact, then extend the elbows to return.

name: JM Press
description: A barbell triceps exercise combining elements of a close-grip press and an elbow extension.
instructions: Use a light load, rack safeties, and a secure close grip. Bend the elbows as the bar approaches the upper chest or chin area without touching the throat, then extend the elbows; avoid turning it into a full bench press.

name: Bodyweight Triceps Extension
description: An elbow extension performed against a secured bar or elevated support.
instructions: Place the hands on a stable support and keep the body aligned. Bend the elbows to move the forehead toward the support, then straighten the arms without bending through the hips.

name: Banded Triceps Pushdown
description: A pushdown using a securely anchored resistance band.
instructions: Fix the band overhead and hold it with stable wrists. Extend the elbows with the upper arms close to the torso, then return without letting the band snap upward.

name: Dumbbell Wrist Curl
description: A wrist-flexion exercise with the forearm supported and palm facing upward.
instructions: Rest the forearm on a bench or thigh with the hand beyond the edge. Curl the wrist upward around the dumbbell, then lower slowly without moving the whole forearm.

name: Barbell Wrist Curl
description: A bilateral wrist curl using a barbell with palms facing upward.
instructions: Support both forearms and let the wrists move freely beyond the support. Flex the wrists to lift the bar, then lower without letting it roll out of a secure grip.

name: Dumbbell Reverse Wrist Curl
description: A supported wrist-extension exercise with the palm facing downward.
instructions: Rest the forearm palm-down with the hand beyond the support. Lift the back of the hand without raising the elbow, then lower the light dumbbell smoothly.

name: Barbell Reverse Wrist Curl
description: A bilateral wrist-extension exercise using an overhand barbell grip.
instructions: Support the forearms with the palms down and wrists free to move. Extend the wrists through a comfortable range, then return without swinging or forcing the grip.

name: Wrist Flexion Isometric
description: A static wrist-flexion effort against the opposite hand or another fixed resistance.
instructions: Support the forearm with the wrist near neutral. Try to bend the palm toward the forearm while the other hand prevents movement, then release gradually without holding the breath.

name: Wrist Extension Isometric
description: A static wrist-extension effort against an immovable resistance.
instructions: Support the forearm and keep the wrist near neutral. Press the back of the hand into the other hand without allowing movement, then relax with control.

name: Wrist Radial Deviation
description: A side-to-side wrist movement toward the thumb against light resistance.
instructions: Support the forearm with the thumb facing upward and hold a light lever or dumbbell. Move the wrist toward the thumb side without rotating the forearm, then return slowly.

name: Wrist Ulnar Deviation
description: A wrist movement toward the little-finger side against resistance.
instructions: Support the forearm and use a light lever oriented to resist the movement. Move the hand toward the little-finger side while keeping the forearm still, then return under control.

name: Forearm Pronation
description: A loaded forearm rotation turning the palm downward.
instructions: Support the elbow and hold a light hammer or lever with the wrist straight. Rotate the forearm toward palm-down without moving the upper arm, then return through a comfortable range.

name: Forearm Supination
description: A loaded forearm rotation turning the palm upward.
instructions: Support the elbow and grip a light lever with a neutral wrist. Rotate toward palm-up without swinging the shoulder, then return slowly.

name: Hand Gripper Squeeze
description: Repeated closing of a hand gripper against spring resistance.
instructions: Place the gripper securely in the palm and keep the wrist comfortable. Close the handles with the fingers, then reopen under control rather than letting the spring snap them apart.

name: Putty Grip Squeeze
description: A controlled hand-closing exercise using resistance putty or a soft ball.
instructions: Hold the material in the palm with the wrist near neutral. Close the fingers around it without forcing painful joints, then release and reshape it as needed.

name: Finger Extension with Band
description: Finger opening against a small elastic band.
instructions: Place the band around the fingers and thumb without restricting circulation. Spread the digits against the resistance, then bring them together slowly while keeping the wrist still.

name: Finger Curl
description: Finger flexion around a light weight with the wrist kept relatively still.
instructions: Support the forearm with the palm upward and maintain control of the weight. Let it move slightly toward the fingers, close the fingers to bring it back into the palm, and avoid dropping it.

name: Plate Pinch Hold
description: An isometric grip hold pinching one or more weight plates.
instructions: Select plates that can be held securely and keep the feet clear. Pinch them between the thumb and fingers with the wrist near neutral, then place them down before the grip fails.

name: Dead Hang
description: A static hang from an overhead bar using a controlled shoulder position.
instructions: Grip a secure bar and use a step if needed. Hold the hang without swinging or forcing the shoulders into a painful end range, then return to the step before releasing.

name: Towel Hang
description: A grip hold hanging from towels secured over a bar.
instructions: Check the towel and bar before loading them. Grip both towel ends firmly and hang with a controlled shoulder position, then lower to a support before the hands slip.

name: Barbell Grip Hold
description: A static hold of a barbell at standing lockout.
instructions: Take the bar from a rack or lift it safely with a manageable load. Stand tall and hold a secure grip without shrugging or leaning backward, then set it down before losing control.

name: Wrist Roller
description: A forearm exercise winding and unwinding a suspended weight on a roller.
instructions: Hold the roller in a supported or comfortable arm position. Turn the handles alternately to wind the cord, then reverse slowly without dropping the hanging weight.

name: Thumb Opposition
description: An active thumb movement toward the fingertips or little-finger base.
instructions: Keep the hand supported and move the thumb across the palm toward the selected fingertip. Return smoothly without forcing the thumb joints or compensating by moving the whole wrist.

name: Finger Abduction
description: A finger-spreading exercise, optionally against light elastic resistance.
instructions: Rest the hand comfortably and spread the fingers apart without bending the wrist. Return slowly, using only resistance that allows each finger to remain controlled.

name: Crunch
description: A short-range abdominal curl lifting the shoulders from the floor.
instructions: Lie on your back with the knees bent and hands supported without pulling the head. Bring the ribs toward the pelvis to lift the shoulder blades, then lower smoothly.

name: Cable Crunch
description: A loaded trunk-flexion exercise using an overhead cable.
instructions: Kneel with a secure handle near the head or upper chest. Curl the ribs toward the pelvis without simply sitting the hips backward, then return under control.

name: Stability Ball Crunch
description: An abdominal curl with the lower torso supported on a stability ball.
instructions: Set the feet wide enough for balance and support the back on the ball. Curl the ribs toward the pelvis through a controlled range, then extend back without losing balance or pulling the neck.

name: Reverse Crunch
description: An abdominal curl that lifts and rolls the pelvis toward the rib cage.
instructions: Lie on your back with the hips and knees bent. Use a small pelvic curl to lift the hips slightly, then lower without swinging the legs or dropping the lower back.

name: Sit-Up
description: A trunk-raising exercise combining abdominal flexion and hip flexion.
instructions: Lie with the knees bent and choose a secure foot position. Curl the torso upward under control, then lower without pulling on the neck or throwing the arms for momentum.

name: Decline Sit-Up
description: A sit-up performed on a decline bench with the legs secured.
instructions: Secure the legs and select an angle that allows control. Lower the torso without hanging into an uncomfortable back position, then curl and sit up without jerking on the restraints.

name: Hanging Knee Raise
description: A hanging hip-flexion and pelvic-curl exercise with bent knees.
instructions: Hang from a secure bar with the shoulders controlled. Raise the knees without swinging and add a small pelvic curl, then lower the legs slowly.

name: Hanging Leg Raise
description: A hanging raise using relatively straight legs.
instructions: Begin in a controlled hang and brace the trunk. Lift the legs through the range you can manage without swinging, then lower while maintaining shoulder control.

name: Captain's Chair Knee Raise
description: A bent-knee raise performed with the forearms and back supported.
instructions: Set the forearms on the pads and keep the shoulders supported. Raise the knees toward the torso without swinging, then lower while avoiding a sudden arch in the lower back.

name: Lying Leg Raise
description: A supine hip-flexion exercise with the legs extended or slightly bent.
instructions: Lie on your back and brace so the pelvis remains controlled. Raise and lower the legs only as far as you can without the lower back arching away excessively.

name: V-Up
description: A simultaneous trunk and leg raise bringing the hands toward the feet.
instructions: Start lying long and brace before lifting. Bring the torso and legs toward each other without jerking through the neck, then lower with control rather than collapsing.

name: Bicycle Crunch
description: An alternating abdominal curl combining trunk rotation and leg movement.
instructions: Lift the shoulders slightly and rotate the rib cage toward the opposite bent knee. Alternate smoothly without pulling the head or letting the lower back arch as the other leg extends.

name: Russian Twist
description: A seated trunk-rotation exercise with the feet supported or lightly elevated.
instructions: Sit tall with a small backward lean and hold a manageable load close to the torso. Rotate the rib cage through a controlled range without whipping the arms or forcing the lower back.

name: Dumbbell Side Bend
description: A loaded lateral trunk-flexion exercise.
instructions: Hold one dumbbell by the side and stand evenly. Bend the torso sideways through a small controlled range, then return to upright without twisting or leaning forward.

name: Cable Side Bend
description: A lateral trunk-flexion exercise using a low cable.
instructions: Stand side-on to the pulley with the handle in the near hand. Move through a controlled side bend and return to upright without rotating the shoulders or shifting the hips excessively.

name: Plank
description: A forearm-supported isometric hold resisting trunk extension.
instructions: Place the elbows beneath the shoulders and extend the legs. Maintain alignment between ribs and pelvis, breathe steadily, and end the hold before the lower back sags.

name: Long-Lever Plank
description: A plank with the elbows placed farther forward to increase the trunk demand.
instructions: Start with the forearms slightly ahead of the shoulders and brace. Hold without sagging or flaring the ribs, using only a lever length that allows normal breathing and control.

name: Side Plank
description: An isometric side support resisting lateral trunk flexion.
instructions: Place the elbow below the shoulder and support the body on the forearm and feet. Lift the hips into alignment and hold without rotating or letting the waist collapse.

name: Kneeling Side Plank
description: A side plank with the knees bent and supported on the floor.
instructions: Set the elbow under the shoulder and bend the knees. Lift the hips to align the shoulders, hips, and knees, then hold or lower without rolling forward.

name: Side Plank Hip Lift
description: A side-plank movement raising and lowering the pelvis.
instructions: Establish a stable side support on the forearm. Lower the pelvis a small distance and lift it again through the side of the trunk, without rotating or collapsing the shoulder.

name: Side Plank with Hip Abduction
description: A side plank adding a raise of the upper leg.
instructions: Hold a steady side plank and keep the pelvis stacked. Lift the top leg without rolling the hips backward, then lower it while maintaining the side support.

name: Dead Bug
description: An alternating limb-lowering drill while stabilizing the trunk in a supine position.
instructions: Lie on your back with the hips and knees bent and arms raised. Extend the opposite arm and leg only as far as the trunk stays controlled, then return and alternate.

name: Dead Bug Heel Tap
description: A dead-bug variation lowering one bent leg to tap the heel on the floor.
instructions: Begin with both hips and knees bent. Lower one heel without changing the pelvic position, bring it back, and alternate while breathing steadily.

name: Bird Dog
description: A quadruped drill extending the opposite arm and leg while keeping the trunk steady.
instructions: Start on hands and knees with a neutral trunk. Reach one arm forward and the opposite leg back without turning the pelvis, then return and alternate.

name: Pallof Press
description: A cable anti-rotation exercise pressing the hands away from the chest.
instructions: Stand side-on to a chest-height cable and brace in a stable stance. Extend the arms while resisting the pull to rotate, then bring the hands back without turning toward the stack.

name: Banded Pallof Press
description: A Pallof press using an elastic band instead of a cable.
instructions: Anchor the band securely at chest height and stand side-on. Press the hands forward without turning the torso, then return with the band under control.

name: Half-Kneeling Pallof Press
description: An anti-rotation press performed with one knee on the floor.
instructions: Set a stable half-kneeling position beside the anchor. Press the handle forward while keeping the pelvis and shoulders square, then return without leaning toward the cable.

name: Cable Wood Chop
description: A diagonal cable movement from a high position toward the opposite hip.
instructions: Stand side-on to a high pulley and brace. Draw the handle diagonally across the torso with coordinated hip and trunk movement, allowing the feet to pivot when needed, then return smoothly.

name: Cable Lift
description: A diagonal cable movement from a low position toward the opposite shoulder.
instructions: Set a low pulley and hold the handle with both hands. Move it upward across the body with controlled trunk rotation rather than an arm swing, then lower along the same path.

name: Landmine Rotation
description: A two-handed rotation moving an anchored bar end from side to side.
instructions: Hold the sleeve in front of the body with a secure grip. Guide it through a controlled arc while turning through the hips and feet as needed, then change direction without wrenching the lower back.

name: Ab Wheel Rollout
description: An anti-extension exercise rolling the hands forward while the trunk stays braced.
instructions: Kneel on padding and grip the wheel. Roll forward only as far as the ribs and pelvis stay controlled, then return without letting the lower back sag or pulling sharply through the shoulders.

name: Stability Ball Rollout
description: A supported rollout with the forearms on a stability ball.
instructions: Kneel behind the ball and brace the trunk. Roll the forearms forward to lengthen the body, then return without losing the rib-to-pelvis position.

name: Stir the Pot
description: A forearm plank on a stability ball with small circular arm movements.
instructions: Establish a stable plank with the forearms on the ball. Make small circles while keeping the trunk from twisting or sagging, then reverse direction with control.

name: Body Saw
description: A forearm plank moving the body backward and forward with the feet on sliders.
instructions: Brace in a plank and place the toes on sliders. Glide backward a short distance and return without bending at the hips or losing control of the lower back.

name: Hollow Body Hold
description: A supine isometric hold with the trunk braced and limbs raised off the floor.
instructions: Lift the shoulders and choose bent or straight legs that allow a controlled pelvis. Hold the position without arching the lower back or straining the neck, and breathe throughout.

name: Reverse Plank
description: A face-up straight-body support with the hands behind the torso.
instructions: Place the hands in a comfortable position and extend the legs. Raise the hips until the body forms a controlled line, then hold without forcing shoulder extension or overarching the back.

name: Plank Shoulder Tap
description: A straight-arm plank alternating hand lifts while resisting rotation.
instructions: Set a stable plank with the feet wide enough for control. Lift one hand to touch the opposite shoulder, replace it, and alternate without shifting the hips side to side.

name: Bear Plank
description: A quadruped hold with the knees hovering just above the floor.
instructions: Set the hands under the shoulders and toes under the feet. Lift the knees slightly while keeping the back steady, then hold with normal breathing rather than raising the hips high.

name: Diaphragmatic Breathing
description: A breathing-control drill emphasizing comfortable expansion of the lower rib cage.
instructions: Lie or sit supported and relax the jaw and shoulders. Breathe in gently so the lower ribs expand, then exhale without force or breath-holding; keep the effort comfortable.

name: Side-Lying Hip Abduction
description: A side-lying leg raise emphasizing the lateral hip muscles.
instructions: Lie with the pelvis stacked and the lower leg bent for support. Lift the upper leg without rolling backward or hiking the hip, then lower slowly.

name: Standing Cable Hip Abduction
description: A standing outward leg movement against an ankle cable.
instructions: Attach the cuff securely and hold a stable support. Move the working leg outward without leaning the torso or turning the pelvis, then return under control.

name: Lateral Band Walk
description: Side-stepping against a loop band while keeping the pelvis controlled.
instructions: Place the band at the prescribed position and take a shallow athletic stance. Step sideways without dragging the trailing foot inward or letting the knees collapse, then continue with controlled spacing.

name: Monster Walk
description: Diagonal forward or backward steps against a resistance band.
instructions: Set a loop band securely and maintain a slight hip and knee bend. Step diagonally while keeping tension and trunk control, then bring the other foot through without snapping the legs together.

name: Clamshell
description: A side-lying hip-rotation exercise opening the upper knee while the feet stay together.
instructions: Lie on your side with the hips and knees bent and pelvis stacked. Open the top knee without rolling the trunk backward, then lower it slowly.

name: Banded Clamshell
description: A clamshell with a resistance band around the thighs.
instructions: Set the band above the knees and lie with the pelvis stacked. Open the top knee against the band while keeping the feet together, then close with control.

name: Reverse Clamshell
description: A side-lying hip internal-rotation exercise lifting the upper foot while the knees remain together.
instructions: Lie with the hips and knees bent and keep the knees stacked. Rotate the top foot upward without moving the pelvis, then lower slowly through a comfortable range.

name: Seated Hip Internal Rotation
description: A seated hip-rotation drill moving the foot outward while the thigh stays steady.
instructions: Sit with the knees bent and pelvis level. Move one foot outward to rotate the hip inward without shifting the knee sideways, then return; add light resistance only when the motion is controlled.

name: Seated Hip External Rotation
description: A seated hip-rotation drill moving the foot inward while the thigh stays steady.
instructions: Sit with the knees bent and the pelvis supported. Rotate one foot inward without moving the whole thigh across the seat, then return smoothly against any prescribed resistance.

name: Standing Hip Hike
description: A single-leg pelvic-control exercise performed on a low step.
instructions: Stand on one leg with the other foot hanging off the step. Lower the free side of the pelvis slightly, then bring the pelvis level without bending the stance knee or leaning the torso.

name: Single-Leg Balance
description: A static balance exercise on one foot.
instructions: Stand near a support, lift one foot, and keep the stance knee softly unlocked. Maintain pressure through the heel and forefoot without gripping the floor excessively or dropping the pelvis.

name: Single-Leg Balance Reach
description: A single-leg balance task with the free foot reaching in different directions.
instructions: Stand near support and maintain a steady pelvis. Reach the free foot forward, sideways, or backward without transferring weight onto it, then return to center under control.

name: Hip Airplane
description: A single-leg hinge with controlled opening and closing of the pelvis.
instructions: Hinge on one leg and use hand support if needed. Rotate the pelvis over the stance hip while keeping the spine controlled, then return without collapsing the knee or twisting abruptly.

name: Side-Lying Hip Adduction
description: An inner-thigh raise with the lower leg acting as the working leg.
instructions: Lie on your side and place the upper foot in front for support. Lift the lower leg toward the upper leg without rolling the pelvis, then lower slowly.

name: Standing Cable Hip Adduction
description: A standing inward leg movement against ankle-cable resistance.
instructions: Secure the cuff and hold a stable support. Draw the working leg inward across a small comfortable range without turning the pelvis, then return against the cable.

name: Adductor Squeeze
description: An isometric inner-thigh squeeze against a ball or pad.
instructions: Place a soft ball or pad between the knees in a supported position. Press inward without forcing the hips or holding the breath, then release the pressure gradually.

name: Short-Lever Copenhagen Plank
description: A side support with the upper knee on a bench, loading the hip adductors.
instructions: Support the upper knee on a stable padded bench and the lower forearm on the floor. Lift the pelvis into alignment, keeping the lower leg off the floor, then hold or lower with control.

name: Long-Lever Copenhagen Plank
description: A side support with the upper ankle or lower leg on a bench.
instructions: Use a stable padded support and place the upper ankle or lower leg on it. Lift the pelvis into a straight-body position while controlling the shoulder, then lower without dropping the hips.

name: Copenhagen Adduction
description: A dynamic side-supported adductor exercise raising the pelvis and lower leg toward the supported upper leg.
instructions: Support the upper leg on a stable bench or with a trained partner. Raise the body and bring the lower leg toward the upper leg, then lower both under control without twisting.

name: Standing Cable Hip Flexion
description: A resisted knee drive using an ankle cuff attached to a low cable.
instructions: Face away from the pulley with a stable support nearby. Lift the knee forward without leaning back or turning the pelvis, then lower slowly.

name: Banded Psoas March
description: An alternating hip-flexion drill against a loop band around the feet.
instructions: Stand supported or lie supine as prescribed, with the band secure around the feet. Lift one knee while the other leg anchors the band, keeping the pelvis controlled, then alternate.

name: Seated Hip Flexion Lift-Off
description: An active hip-flexion exercise lifting the foot while sitting upright.
instructions: Sit on a stable surface with the torso tall. Lift one knee and foot a small distance without leaning backward or pushing through the hands, then lower with control.

name: Straight-Leg Raise
description: A supine leg raise keeping the working knee extended.
instructions: Bend the nonworking knee for support and tighten the working thigh. Raise the straight leg without arching the back, then lower slowly while keeping the knee controlled.

name: Banded Terminal Knee Extension
description: A standing knee-extension exercise against a band behind the knee.
instructions: Anchor the band securely behind the working knee and begin with a small knee bend. Straighten the knee with the foot grounded without forceful hyperextension, then bend it again slowly.

name: Short-Arc Knee Extension
description: A supported knee extension over a small bolster.
instructions: Lie with a rolled towel or bolster under the knee. Tighten the thigh to lift the heel and straighten the knee through the available range, then lower gently.

name: Standing Calf Raise
description: A heel raise performed standing with relatively straight knees.
instructions: Hold a stable support if needed and keep pressure through the forefoot. Lift the heels without rolling the ankles outward, then lower slowly through a comfortable range.

name: Single-Leg Calf Raise
description: A standing heel raise performed on one leg.
instructions: Hold a support lightly and lift the free foot. Rise through the working forefoot with the knee controlled, then lower without bouncing or letting the ankle collapse.

name: Dumbbell Calf Raise
description: A standing calf raise holding dumbbells for added load.
instructions: Hold the weights securely and use a stable support or level surface. Raise the heels while keeping the knees relatively straight, then lower with the load controlled.

name: Seated Dumbbell Calf Raise
description: A bent-knee calf raise with a dumbbell supported over the thigh.
instructions: Sit with the foot flat or forefoot on a stable support and hold the dumbbell above the knee. Raise and lower the heel while keeping the knee bent and the weight secure.

name: Bent-Knee Standing Calf Raise
description: A standing calf raise while maintaining a slight knee bend.
instructions: Hold a support and bend the knees to the prescribed angle. Keep that angle as you raise and lower the heels, avoiding a repeated squat or ankle wobble.

name: Eccentric Heel Lower
description: A calf exercise using assistance to rise and one leg to control the lowering phase.
instructions: Rise onto the forefeet using both legs or support, then shift to the working leg. Lower the heel slowly through the prescribed range and reset with assistance rather than bouncing.

name: Calf Raise Isometric
description: A static hold in a raised-heel position.
instructions: Rise onto the forefeet using stable support if needed. Hold the selected heel height without rolling the ankles or locking the knees forcefully, then lower with control.

name: Tibialis Raise
description: An ankle-dorsiflexion exercise lifting the forefeet while the heels remain supported.
instructions: Stand with the back against a wall or sit with support. Keep the heels grounded, lift the toes and forefeet toward the shins, then lower without snapping them down.

name: Banded Ankle Dorsiflexion
description: Pulling the forefoot toward the shin against a resistance band.
instructions: Secure the band in front of the foot and support the leg. Lift the forefoot toward the shin without rotating the hip or knee, then return slowly.

name: Banded Ankle Plantar Flexion
description: Pressing the forefoot away from the shin against a band.
instructions: Sit with the leg supported and the band around the ball of the foot. Point the foot away while keeping the ankle aligned, then return under control.

name: Banded Ankle Inversion
description: Turning the sole inward against light band resistance.
instructions: Support the leg and position the band to resist inward foot movement. Turn the sole inward without rotating the whole leg, then return through a comfortable ankle range.

name: Banded Ankle Eversion
description: Turning the sole outward against light band resistance.
instructions: Stabilize the lower leg and set the band to resist outward movement. Move the outer border of the foot outward without turning the knee, then return slowly.

name: Short-Foot Exercise
description: An active foot-arch exercise without curling the toes.
instructions: Keep the heel and forefoot on the floor. Gently draw the ball of the foot toward the heel to raise the arch, keeping the toes long, then release without rolling onto the outer foot.

name: Toe Yoga
description: A toe-control drill separating big-toe movement from the other toes.
instructions: Keep the foot supported and lift the big toe while the smaller toes stay down. Reverse the pattern without moving the ankle excessively, using a comfortable range.

name: Towel Toe Curl
description: A toe-flexion exercise pulling a towel toward the foot.
instructions: Sit with the heel on the floor and a towel beneath the toes. Curl the toes to gather the towel without lifting the heel, then relax and repeat with control.

name: Resisted Big-Toe Flexion
description: A big-toe press against light resistance while the foot remains supported.
instructions: Place a band or suitable resistance over the big toe. Press the toe down without rolling the ankle or gripping excessively with the other toes, then release slowly.

name: Resisted Big-Toe Extension
description: A big-toe lift against light elastic resistance.
instructions: Stabilize the foot and place a light band so it resists lifting the big toe. Raise the toe without moving the ankle, then lower under control.

name: Toe Spread
description: An active exercise spreading the toes while the foot stays supported.
instructions: Place the foot flat and gently spread the toes apart. Keep the heel and forefoot grounded and avoid curling the toes, then relax them back to the starting position.

name: Heel Walk
description: Walking on the heels with the forefeet lifted.
instructions: Stand near support, raise the forefeet, and take short controlled steps on the heels. Keep the toes clear without leaning excessively backward, then lower the feet normally.

name: Toe Walk
description: Walking on the forefeet while maintaining an elevated heel position.
instructions: Rise onto the balls of the feet and take short, balanced steps. Keep the ankles aligned and avoid letting the heels drop suddenly, then return to normal standing.

name: Supine Chin Nod
description: A small nodding movement with the head supported on the floor or a pillow.
instructions: Lie comfortably and gently nod as though making a small yes movement. Keep the head resting on its support and avoid forcing the chin hard into the chest or holding the breath.

name: Chin Retraction
description: A controlled backward glide of the head while keeping the face level.
instructions: Sit or stand tall and gently move the head backward as if making a small double chin. Keep the eyes level, avoid tipping the head, and return without forcing the end range.

name: Neck Flexion Isometric
description: A gentle static neck-flexion effort against the hand.
instructions: Sit supported with the head near neutral and place the palm on the forehead. Press lightly into the hand without moving the head, then release; stop if dizziness or radiating symptoms occur.

name: Neck Extension Isometric
description: A gentle static neck-extension effort against a hand or padded support.
instructions: Keep the head near neutral and support the back of the head. Press backward lightly without extending the neck or holding the breath, then release slowly.

name: Neck Lateral Flexion Isometric
description: A static side-bending effort of the neck against the hand.
instructions: Sit with the shoulders relaxed and place a hand against the side of the head. Press gently sideways without moving or rotating the head, then release and repeat on the other side as prescribed.

name: Neck Rotation Isometric
description: A static neck-rotation effort against the hand.
instructions: Place the hand against the side of the forehead and keep the head centered. Attempt a gentle turn while the hand prevents motion, then release without forcing the jaw or neck.

name: Active Neck Rotation
description: Controlled turning of the head through an available, comfortable range.
instructions: Sit tall with the shoulders relaxed. Turn the head slowly to one side without tilting or forcing the end range, return to center, and repeat to the other side.

name: Clean
description: A barbell lift from the floor to the front shoulders, received in a squat.
instructions: Set a stable start over the bar, push through the floor, and keep the bar close as the legs and hips extend. Move under into a secure front rack, stand from the receiving squat, and lower safely. Learn the movement with qualified coaching.

name: Power Clean
description: A clean received above a full squat position.
instructions: Lift the bar close to the body and accelerate through the legs and hips. Move under into a balanced partial squat with the elbows forward, stand, and reset without allowing the bar to crash onto the wrists.

name: Hang Clean
description: A clean starting from a prescribed hang position rather than the floor.
instructions: Lift the bar to standing and hinge to the assigned hang height. Extend through the legs and hips, move under into a secure front rack, and stand from the receiving squat.

name: Hang Power Clean
description: A hang clean received in a partial squat.
instructions: Start from the prescribed hang position with the bar close. Accelerate through the hips and knees, receive on the front shoulders above a full squat, then stand and reset with control.

name: Block Clean
description: A clean starting from blocks at a prescribed bar height.
instructions: Set stable blocks and position the bar evenly. Establish tension before lifting, accelerate through the legs and hips, then move under to receive the bar securely on the shoulders.

name: Muscle Clean
description: A clean turnover performed without dropping into a receiving squat.
instructions: Use a light bar and drive upward from the prescribed start. Keep the bar close and rotate the elbows into the front rack without re-bending the knees to catch it.

name: Clean Pull
description: A weightlifting pull using a clean grip without catching the bar on the shoulders.
instructions: Set up as for a clean and push the floor away with the bar close. Extend the legs and hips to finish tall, letting the arms guide rather than curl the bar, then lower safely.

name: Clean High Pull
description: A clean-grip pull that continues with an upward elbow action after leg and hip extension.
instructions: Accelerate the bar with the lower body while keeping it close. After extension, guide the elbows upward and outward without leaning backward, then lower with control.

name: Snatch
description: A wide-grip barbell lift from the floor to an overhead squat.
instructions: Set a stable wide grip and keep the bar close through the pull. Extend the legs and hips, move under to receive overhead with straight elbows, then stand only after balance is established. Practice under qualified coaching.

name: Power Snatch
description: A snatch received overhead above a full squat.
instructions: Pull the bar close from the floor and accelerate with the legs and hips. Move under into a controlled partial squat with the bar overhead, then stand and return the bar safely.

name: Hang Snatch
description: A snatch beginning from a prescribed hang position.
instructions: Stand with a wide grip, hinge to the assigned hang height, and keep the bar close. Extend and move under into an overhead receiving squat, then stand with the bar balanced.

name: Hang Power Snatch
description: A hang snatch caught overhead in a partial squat.
instructions: Lower the bar to the prescribed hang height with a controlled hinge. Accelerate through the legs and hips, catch overhead above a full squat, then stand before resetting.

name: Block Snatch
description: A snatch beginning with the bar supported on blocks.
instructions: Set secure blocks at equal height and establish tension before moving. Drive the bar upward close to the body, receive in a stable overhead squat, and stand with control.

name: Muscle Snatch
description: A snatch turnover completed without re-bending the knees to receive the bar.
instructions: Use a light load and a wide grip. Extend the legs and hips, continue the upward pull, and turn the bar overhead without a receiving dip or forceful lower-back lean.

name: Snatch Pull
description: A wide-grip weightlifting pull without an overhead catch.
instructions: Begin in a snatch start position and push through the floor. Keep the bar close as the legs and hips extend, finish tall without pulling backward, and return under control.

name: Snatch High Pull
description: A snatch-grip pull with the elbows lifting after lower-body extension.
instructions: Pull close from the assigned starting position and extend the hips and knees. Guide the elbows high and outward while keeping the bar close, then lower without wrenching the shoulders.

name: Snatch Balance
description: An overhead receiving drill dropping from a back-rack position into an overhead squat.
instructions: Use a light bar, clear space, and an established safe bail technique. Dip and drive the bar upward from the upper back, move into an overhead squat, and stabilize before standing.

name: Push Press
description: An overhead barbell press assisted by a coordinated leg dip and drive.
instructions: Support the bar at the shoulders and make a short controlled dip with an upright trunk. Drive through the legs into the press, finish overhead without re-bending the knees to receive, and lower safely.

name: Dumbbell Push Press
description: A dumbbell overhead press assisted by leg drive.
instructions: Hold the dumbbells at the shoulders and brace. Dip slightly, drive through the legs, and continue pressing overhead, then lower to the shoulders with the weights controlled.

name: Push Jerk
description: A barbell overhead lift using a dip, drive, and second knee bend to receive the bar.
instructions: Start from the front rack, dip vertically, and drive the bar upward. Re-bend the knees to receive with straight elbows, stabilize, then stand before lowering.

name: Split Jerk
description: An overhead lift received in a split stance after a leg-driven bar acceleration.
instructions: Dip and drive from the front rack, then move under into a balanced split with the arms straight. Stabilize overhead, recover the feet in controlled steps, and lower using a practiced safe method.

name: Clean and Jerk
description: A two-part lift combining a clean to the shoulders with a jerk overhead.
instructions: Clean the bar into a secure front rack and stand. Reset the stance and brace, perform the chosen jerk technique, stabilize overhead, then lower or release only in a suitable lifting area.

name: Dumbbell Snatch
description: A one-arm lift bringing a dumbbell from the floor to overhead in one movement.
instructions: Start over the dumbbell with a stable trunk. Extend the legs and hips, guide the weight close, and receive it overhead with control before lowering safely.

name: Kettlebell Swing
description: A two-handed hip-driven kettlebell swing to approximately chest height.
instructions: Hike the bell between the legs from a stable hinge. Extend the hips to let it float forward without lifting mainly through the arms, then hinge as it returns and park it safely after the final repetition.

name: Single-Arm Kettlebell Swing
description: A one-arm hip-driven kettlebell swing that adds an anti-rotation demand.
instructions: Hike the bell with one hand and keep the shoulders and hips controlled. Drive through the hips, let the bell float, then absorb its return with a hinge rather than a twist.

name: Double Kettlebell Swing
description: A swing performed with one kettlebell in each hand.
instructions: Use enough stance width for both bells to pass safely. Hike them together, extend the hips to drive the swing, and guide them back without colliding the bells or rounding the trunk.

name: Kettlebell Clean
description: A one-arm kettlebell lift ending in a controlled front-rack position.
instructions: Drive the bell from a hinge and keep its path close to the body. Guide the hand through the handle to receive the bell softly at the forearm and upper arm, then return without letting it slam the wrist.

name: Kettlebell Snatch
description: A one-arm ballistic kettlebell lift received overhead.
instructions: Drive from the hips and keep the bell on a controlled path. Guide the hand into the handle as it reaches overhead rather than letting it flip onto the wrist, then lower using a practiced controlled return.

name: Kettlebell Clean and Press
description: A kettlebell clean followed by a strict overhead press.
instructions: Clean the bell smoothly to the rack and settle the body. Press overhead without a leg dip, return to the rack, then lower safely before repeating.

name: Thruster
description: A front squat linked directly to an overhead press.
instructions: Hold the bar in the front rack, squat with a stable torso, and drive upward. Continue the leg drive into an overhead press, then return to the rack before the next controlled squat.

name: Dumbbell Thruster
description: A front squat and overhead press combined using dumbbells.
instructions: Hold the dumbbells at the shoulders and lower into a controlled squat. Stand powerfully into the press, then bring the weights back to the shoulders before descending again.

name: Turkish Get-Up
description: A staged floor-to-standing movement while stabilizing a weight overhead.
instructions: Begin with a light weight and a straight supporting arm. Move through a controlled roll, hand support, leg sweep, half-kneeling position, and stand; reverse the sequence without losing overhead alignment. Learn the stages before adding load.

name: Kettlebell Windmill
description: A controlled hip hinge and sideward reach while holding a kettlebell overhead.
instructions: Establish a stable overhead hold and a comfortable foot angle. Shift the hips back and guide the free hand down the leg, keeping the loaded arm controlled, then return without forcing rotation.

name: Farmer's Carry
description: A loaded walk holding weights beside both legs.
instructions: Lift the implements safely, stand tall, and walk with short controlled steps. Keep the loads clear of the legs and place them down before grip or posture fails.

name: Suitcase Carry
description: A loaded walk holding a weight on one side.
instructions: Pick up one weight and stand without leaning away from it. Walk with even steps while keeping the shoulders and pelvis level, then set the weight down with control.

name: Front-Rack Carry
description: A loaded walk with weights held at the front shoulders.
instructions: Secure the dumbbells or kettlebells in the rack position. Walk without losing the rib-to-pelvis alignment or letting the weights drift away, then lower them using a controlled transition.

name: Single-Arm Front-Rack Carry
description: A front-rack carry with a weight on one side.
instructions: Rack the weight close to the shoulder and stabilize the wrist. Walk without rotating or leaning sideways, then return the weight safely before changing sides.

name: Overhead Carry
description: A walk while stabilizing one or two weights overhead.
instructions: Establish a stable overhead position before stepping. Walk slowly with the ribs controlled and shoulders free to support the overhead load, then stop before balance or elbow position deteriorates.

name: Waiter's Carry
description: A one-arm overhead carry with the trunk resisting side bending.
instructions: Hold a manageable weight securely overhead. Walk with the arm stacked and torso upright without bending away from the weight, then lower only after stopping.

name: Bottoms-Up Kettlebell Carry
description: A walk holding an inverted kettlebell in the rack position.
instructions: Establish a steady bottoms-up hold with the bell above the handle. Walk slowly while keeping the wrist and elbow controlled, and set the bell down before it tips.

name: Sandbag Bear-Hug Carry
description: A loaded walk hugging a sandbag against the torso.
instructions: Lift the bag with a controlled squat or hinge and hold it close to the chest. Walk with short steps without leaning backward, then lower the bag safely.

name: Zercher Carry
description: A loaded walk holding a bar in the elbow creases.
instructions: Take the bar from an appropriate rack height and keep it close. Walk with the trunk braced and the elbows controlled, then return the bar to the rack rather than dropping it from the arms.

name: Yoke Walk
description: A loaded carry with a strongman yoke supported across the upper back.
instructions: Set the crossbar height and clear the route. Stand beneath the yoke, brace, lift it clear, and take short deliberate steps before setting it down evenly.

name: Sled Push
description: A forward drive against a weighted sled using fixed handles.
instructions: Grip the handles, brace, and lean from the ankles as appropriate for the load. Drive through alternating steps without collapsing the trunk, keeping the route clear.

name: Backward Sled Drag
description: A backward walk pulling a sled through straps or handles.
instructions: Take up slack in the straps and maintain a stable torso. Step backward in short controlled steps, extending the knees against the load without stumbling or letting the straps pull you off balance.

name: Forward Sled Drag
description: A forward walk against a sled attached through a belt or harness.
instructions: Secure the attachment and keep the line clear of the legs. Lean into a controlled walk and push the ground backward, then slow gradually rather than stopping abruptly.

name: Lateral Sled Drag
description: A side-stepping sled drag against resistance at the hips or hands.
instructions: Set a secure attachment and face sideways to the direction of travel. Step laterally without crossing the feet or twisting the knees, maintaining a controlled pelvis and trunk.

name: Sled Row
description: A standing or supported row that draws a sled toward the body through handles.
instructions: Take up slack with the arms extended and brace the trunk. Pull the handles toward the ribs without jerking the back, then reset your position safely for the next pull.

name: Rope Sled Pull
description: A hand-over-hand rope pull drawing a sled toward a stable seated or standing position.
instructions: Anchor the body with a firm stance or seat and keep the rope path clear. Pull hand over hand without wrapping the rope around the hands, then gather slack away from the feet.

name: Squat Jump
description: A vertical jump beginning from a held squat position without a preparatory countermovement.
instructions: Settle into a stable partial squat and briefly hold the starting position. Jump upward without an extra downward dip, then land with the hips and knees bending together and reset before repeating.

name: Countermovement Jump
description: A vertical jump using a quick downward movement immediately before takeoff.
instructions: Stand tall, dip briefly, and reverse direction into a vertical jump. Use a consistent arm strategy and absorb the landing under control without collapsing the knees inward.

name: Box Jump
description: A jump from the floor onto a stable raised box.
instructions: Select a box you can land on without extreme knee tucking. Jump onto it with both feet fully supported, absorb the landing, stand tall, and step down rather than jumping blindly off.

name: Broad Jump
description: A standing horizontal jump landing on both feet.
instructions: Start with a stable stance and load the hips with an arm swing. Jump forward into a clear landing area, absorb through the hips and knees, and establish balance before resetting.

name: Split Squat Jump
description: A jump from a split stance, optionally switching legs in the air.
instructions: Begin in a balanced split stance and lower slightly. Jump vertically, land with both knees controlled in a stable split, and reset or switch only as prescribed.

name: Lateral Bound
description: A side-to-side jump landing primarily on one leg.
instructions: Push sideways from one foot and land on the other with the hip and knee flexed. Stabilize the pelvis and knee before bounding back or continuing according to the drill.

name: Pogo Jump
description: A series of small vertical rebounds driven mainly through the ankles.
instructions: Stand tall with softly unlocked knees. Make low rhythmic jumps from the forefeet, keeping the contacts controlled and ending the set before the landings become heavy.

name: Single-Leg Pogo
description: A low-amplitude hopping drill performed on one foot.
instructions: Stand on one leg near support if needed. Make small controlled ankle-driven hops, keeping the knee aligned and pelvis steady, then stop before losing rhythm or balance.

name: Lateral Line Hop
description: Small repeated jumps side to side over a floor line.
instructions: Mark a clear line and keep the jumps low. Move across it with controlled foot contacts and stable knees, maintaining balance rather than chasing distance.

name: Drop Landing
description: A landing-control drill stepping from a low platform without an immediate rebound.
instructions: Step off a suitable low box into a clear area. Land on both feet, bend the hips and knees to absorb the drop, and hold a stable finish before resetting.

name: Depth Jump
description: An advanced drop followed by an immediate controlled vertical rebound.
instructions: Use a low platform appropriate to your landing ability and a clear area. Step off, absorb the contact, and rebound upward without a prolonged collapse, then land and reset; use qualified coaching.

name: Lateral Box Jump
description: A sideways jump onto a low stable box.
instructions: Stand beside the box and load the hips and knees. Jump sideways onto the surface with both feet supported, stabilize, and step down before repeating.

name: Plyometric Push-Up
description: A push-up with enough upward acceleration for the hands to leave the support briefly.
instructions: Begin from a stable plank or elevated support. Lower with control, push explosively, and catch the landing with soft elbows while keeping the trunk aligned.

name: Medicine Ball Chest Pass
description: A two-handed forward throw from the chest.
instructions: Face a safe wall or prepared partner with the ball near the chest. Drive the arms forward to release it, then receive the return with yielding elbows or retrieve it before resetting.

name: Seated Medicine Ball Chest Throw
description: A chest throw performed seated to limit assistance from the legs.
instructions: Sit against a stable back support with a clear throwing area. Hold the ball at the chest and project it forward with the arms, keeping the torso supported rather than leaning into the throw.

name: Medicine Ball Overhead Slam
description: An overhead-to-floor throw using a ball designed for slamming.
instructions: Check that the ball and floor are suitable and keep the area clear. Raise the ball overhead, drive it down with coordinated trunk and arm action, and retrieve it without putting the face over a rebound.

name: Medicine Ball Rotational Throw
description: A side-on throw driven by coordinated hip and trunk rotation.
instructions: Stand side-on to a suitable wall or partner. Load the rear hip, rotate through the hips and torso while allowing the feet to pivot, and release the ball without twisting against a fixed knee.

name: Medicine Ball Scoop Toss
description: An underhand throw using leg and hip extension.
instructions: Hold the ball low with a braced torso and hinge slightly. Extend the legs and hips to project the ball forward into a clear area, then reset without chasing an unsafe rebound.

name: Medicine Ball Overhead Backward Throw
description: A backward overhead throw powered by leg and hip extension.
instructions: Check that the landing area behind you is completely clear. Dip with the ball held low, extend upward, and release overhead behind the body without forcing the lower back into hyperextension.

name: Wall Ball
description: A front squat linked to an upward medicine ball throw at a wall target.
instructions: Hold the ball near the chest, squat under control, and stand into an upward throw. Receive the returning ball with soft arms and knees, maintaining space from other users.

name: Walking
description: Continuous walking on level ground at the prescribed pace.
instructions: Walk with comfortable, even steps and natural arm movement. Keep the route clear and adjust speed so posture and footing remain controlled.

name: Incline Treadmill Walk
description: Walking uphill on a treadmill at a selected incline.
instructions: Attach the safety clip and begin at a manageable speed. Walk without hanging on the handrails, adjust the incline gradually, and slow the belt before stepping off.

name: Running
description: Continuous running at a prescribed pace or effort.
instructions: Use a clear route and increase speed gradually. Keep the stride controlled and shoulders relaxed, adjusting pace when fatigue makes the movement unstable.

name: Sprint
description: A high-speed running effort over a prescribed distance or duration.
instructions: Use a suitable surface, clear run-out space, and a progressive warm-up. Accelerate smoothly, maintain controlled mechanics, and decelerate over enough distance rather than stopping suddenly.

name: Stationary Bike
description: Cycling on an indoor bike for conditioning.
instructions: Adjust the saddle and handlebar positions so the hips remain steady while pedaling. Start with manageable resistance, pedal smoothly, and reduce effort before dismounting.

name: Air Bike
description: Conditioning on a fan-resistance bike using both arms and legs.
instructions: Adjust the seat and begin pedaling while pushing and pulling the handles. Coordinate the limbs without rocking excessively, then reduce speed before letting go or stepping off.

name: Rowing Ergometer
description: Repeated rowing strokes on an indoor rowing machine.
instructions: Secure the feet, drive first through the legs, then open the hips and pull the handle toward the lower ribs. Return by extending the arms, hinging forward, and bending the knees in sequence.

name: Ski Ergometer
description: Repeated downward pulling strokes on a ski ergometer.
instructions: Stand balanced with the hands above shoulder level. Drive the handles down with coordinated trunk and hip movement, finish with the arms near the thighs, and return upward under control.

name: Elliptical Trainer
description: Continuous stepping on an elliptical machine, with optional moving handles.
instructions: Step onto the stationary pedals carefully and choose a manageable resistance. Move smoothly through the stride without bouncing or hanging on the handles, then slow fully before dismounting.

name: Stair Climber
description: Repeated stepping on a rotating-stair or stepper machine.
instructions: Start slowly and place enough of each foot on the step for support. Climb without hanging bodyweight from the rails, then use the controls to stop before stepping off.

name: Jump Rope
description: Repeated low jumps timed to a rotating rope.
instructions: Use a clear area and a rope of suitable length. Turn mainly through the wrists, make low balanced jumps, and land softly without lifting the knees higher than needed.

name: Double-Under
description: A jump-rope variation with two rope rotations per jump.
instructions: Establish controlled single jumps first. Jump slightly higher while accelerating the rope through the wrists, keep the body aligned, and reset if the timing becomes uncontrolled.

name: Battle Rope Waves
description: Repeated arm-driven waves sent along anchored battle ropes.
instructions: Anchor the ropes securely and take a stable athletic stance. Create alternating waves with controlled arm movement while keeping the torso steady, then reduce the motion before releasing the ropes.

name: Battle Rope Slams
description: Simultaneous rope lifts and forceful downward waves using the arms and trunk.
instructions: Hold the anchored ropes with a stable stance. Lift both handles, drive them down with controlled trunk and leg contribution, and repeat without rounding or jerking under fatigue.

name: Burpee
description: A floor-to-standing conditioning movement combining a plank, push-up, and vertical jump.
instructions: Place the hands on the floor and move the feet back into a controlled plank. Perform a push-up, bring the feet toward the hands, and jump upward; absorb the landing and reset before repeating.

name: Mountain Climber
description: An alternating knee drive from a straight-arm plank.
instructions: Set the hands under the shoulders and brace. Bring one knee forward, return it, and alternate without bouncing the hips or letting the lower back sag.

name: Bear Crawl
description: A low crawl on the hands and feet with the knees hovering.
instructions: Start with the knees just off the floor and a stable trunk. Move opposite hand and foot in short steps without swaying excessively, keeping the path clear.

name: Crab Walk
description: A face-up crawl supported by the hands and feet.
instructions: Place the hands behind the body in a comfortable shoulder position and lift the hips slightly. Take controlled steps without forcing shoulder extension or dropping the pelvis abruptly.

name: Shuttle Run
description: Repeated short runs between two marked points.
instructions: Set clear markers and enough space to slow down. Run to each mark, decelerate with controlled steps, turn without twisting on a rigid knee, and accelerate back.

name: Lateral Shuffle
description: Sideways locomotion using repeated push-off steps without crossing the feet.
instructions: Take an athletic stance and move sideways with short steps. Keep the feet from crossing and control the trunk when stopping or changing direction.
